14	// Init loads the source, if there is one.
15	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
16		if m.source == nil {
17			return nil
18		}
19		return tea.Batch(loadCmd(m.source), m.spinner.Tick)
20	}
21	
22	// loadCmd fetches a source's content. Every read the viewer does goes through
23	// here, on a command's goroutine — Update does no I/O (Rule 110).
24	func loadCmd(source viewer.Source) tea.Cmd {
25		return func() tea.Msg {
26			data, err := source.Load()
27			return DocumentLoadedMsg{
28				Name:    source.Name(),
29				Kind:    source.Kind(),
30				Content: data,
31				Err:     err,
32			}
33		}
34	}
35	
36	// followTickMsg asks for the next read of a followed source. It carries the
37	// generation it was started for, so a loop the user has stopped cannot
38	// resurrect itself — see stopFollowing.
39	type followTickMsg struct{ gen int }
40	
41	func followTickCmd(every time.Duration, gen int) tea.Cmd {
42		// A non-positive interval would make tea.Tick fire without pausing and spin
43		// one docker exec per frame. Refused here rather than trusted, the way the
44		// ports tab refuses a hand-edited 0.
45		if every <= 0 {
46			every = defaultFollowInterval
47		}
48		return tea.Tick(every, func(time.Time) tea.Msg { return followTickMsg{gen: gen} })
49	}
50	
51	// defaultFollowInterval is the floor a source with no sensible answer falls to.
52	const defaultFollowInterval = 2 * time.Second
53	
54	// InEditMode keeps command mode out while a field has the keyboard: the search
55	// box, or the go-to-line prompt.
56	func (m Model) InEditMode() bool { return m.bar.InEditMode() || m.gotoActive }
57	
58	// FilterBarVisible tells the router to close the viewport border into the bar
59	// (Rule 136).
60	func (m Model) FilterBarVisible() bool {
61		// Every display but the tree is text, and the search belongs to all of
62		// them: a rendered Markdown is searched on what it shows, which is the only
63		// answer that agrees with the screen.
64		//
65		// The go-to-line prompt takes the same slot, so it closes the border the
66		// same way — and the footer stands at the same height whether the prompt
67		// opened over an active search or over nothing.
68		return (m.bar.IsVisible() || m.gotoActive) && m.display != displayTree

72		switch msg := msg.(type) {
73		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:

75			return m, nil
76	
77		case tea.KeyMsg:
78			return m.handleKeyMsg(msg)
79	
80		case DocumentLoadedMsg:
81			return m.handleDocumentLoaded(msg)
82	
83		case PagerExitMsg:
84			return m.handlePagerExit(msg)
85	
86		case followTickMsg:
87			return m.handleFollowTick(msg)
88	
89		case spinner.TickMsg:

91			if !m.loading {

93			}

96			m.footer.SetSpinnerFrame(m.spinner.View())

100		m.footer.Handle(msg)

102	}

120		m.loading = false

123			return m, m.footer.Error(loadErrorMessage(msg.Err))

129	// loadErrorMessage names the two refusals and hides the rest behind the log
130	// (Rule 128): "file is too large" is something the user can act on, an OS error
131	// string in a footer is not.
132	func loadErrorMessage(err error) string {
133		switch err {
134		case viewer.ErrTooLarge:
135			return "File is too large to view"
136		case viewer.ErrBinary:
137			return "Not a text file"
138		default:
139			return "Failed to open — check logs"
140		}
141	}

143	// handlePagerExit takes the pager's return, and says so when it failed.
144	//
145	// The report is not decoration. A pager that cannot start comes back in
146	// milliseconds and looks exactly like one the user quit at once, so the whole
147	// event is indistinguishable from `V` doing nothing — which is precisely how the
148	// broken Windows command line went unnoticed. The log line was already there and
149	// nobody reads a log to find out why a key did nothing.
150	func (m Model) handlePagerExit(msg PagerExitMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
151		var report tea.Cmd
152		if msg.Err != nil {
153			log.Printf("ERROR [viewer] pager: %v", msg.Err)
154			report = m.footer.Error("Pager failed — check logs")
155		}
156		// Whatever the pager showed, the document may have moved on while the TUI
157		// was suspended. Reloading is the only way back to something true.
158		if m.source == nil {
159			return m, report
160		}
161		m.loading = true
162		return m, tea.Batch(report, loadCmd(m.source))
163	}

165	func (m Model) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
166		// The prompt is a mode: it claims every key before the pane sees one, the
167		// way a confirmation modal does, so a digit cannot also scroll and `esc`
168		// closes the prompt rather than leaving the viewer.
169		if m.gotoActive {
170			return m.handleGotoKey(msg)
171		}
172		if m.bar.InEditMode() {
173			var cmd tea.Cmd
174			m.bar, cmd = m.bar.Update(msg)
175			m.rebuildText()
176			return m, cmd
177		}
178	
179		switch msg.String() {
180		case "esc":
181			return m.goBack()
182		case "f":
183			m.toggleDisplay()
184			return m, nil
185		case "c":
186			m.toggleHighlight()
187			return m, nil
188		case "ctrl+r":
189			return m.reload()
190		}
191	
192		if m.display == displayTree {
193			return m.handleTreeKey(msg)
194		}
195		return m.handleTextKey(msg)
196	}
197	
198	// goBack returns to whoever opened the document. With no origin — the empty
199	// viewer the router builds for its own contract test — there is nowhere to go,
200	// and swallowing esc silently is better than switching to a view nobody asked
201	// for.
202	func (m Model) goBack() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
203		if m.OriginView == "" {
204			return m, nil
205		}
206		// Leaving stops the clock. The router keeps this view, so a loop left
207		// running would go on shelling out to docker every two seconds for a
208		// document nobody is looking at — and the user would come back to a pane
209		// that had scrolled itself to the bottom while they were gone.
210		m = m.stopFollowing()
211		origin := m.OriginView
212		return m, func() tea.Msg { return BackToOriginMsg{Origin: origin} }
213	}
214	
215	func (m Model) reload() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
216		if m.source == nil {
217			return m, nil
218		}
219		m.loading = true
220		return m, tea.Batch(loadCmd(m.source), m.spinner.Tick)
221	}
222	
223	func (m Model) handleTreeKey(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
224		switch msg.String() {
225		case "right":
226			m.toggleNode(true)
227			return m, nil
228		case "left":
229			m.toggleNode(false)
230			return m, nil
231		}
232		return m, m.tree.Update(msg)
233	}
234	
235	func (m Model) handleTextKey(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
236		switch msg.String() {
237		case "/":
238			return m, m.bar.ActivateSearch()
239		case "s":
240			m.toggleCaseSensitive()
241			return m, nil
242		case "n":
243			m.toggleLineNumbers()
244			return m, nil
245		case "g":
246			return m, m.activateGoto()
247		case "w":
248			m.wrap = !m.wrap
249			m.rebuildText()
250			return m, nil
251		case "v":
252			if !m.isLog() {
253				return m, nil
254			}
255			m.cycleVerbosity()
256			return m, nil
257		case "t":
258			return m.toggleTimestamps()
259		case keymap.Fetch:
260			return m.toggleFollow()
261		case keymap.Pager:
262			return m.openPager()
263	
264		// The scroll keys. `q` is deliberately absent: it is the application's quit
265		// key (Rule 111), and the logs pane this replaced was the one screen that
266		// swallowed it.
267		case "up":
268			m.textViewport.ScrollUp(1)
269		case "down":
270			m.textViewport.ScrollDown(1)
271		case "pgup":
272			m.textViewport.HalfPageUp()
273		case "pgdown":
274			m.textViewport.HalfPageDown()
275		case "home":
276			m.textViewport.GotoTop()
277		case "end":
278			m.textViewport.GotoBottom()
279		}
280		return m, nil
281	}
282	
283	// ── The source's optional capabilities ───────────────────────────────────────
284	//
285	// Each is probed with a type assertion, the way the router probes FooterView.
286	// They are three single-method interfaces rather than one with three methods
287	// precisely so there is no half-satisfied state: CLAUDE.md's HeaderView warning
288	// is about a view supplying two of four methods and silently satisfying none.
289	
290	// timestamps returns the source's timestamp capability, if it has one.
291	func (m Model) timestamps() (viewer.Timestamped, bool) {
292		src, ok := m.source.(viewer.Timestamped)
293		return src, ok
294	}
295	
296	func (m Model) followable() (viewer.Followable, bool) {
297		src, ok := m.source.(viewer.Followable)
298		return src, ok
299	}
300	
301	func (m Model) pageable() (viewer.Pageable, bool) {
302		src, ok := m.source.(viewer.Pageable)
303		return src, ok
304	}
305	
306	// timestampsOn tracks the toggle rather than asking the source, which holds it
307	// but cannot be interrogated through the interface — WithTimestamps returns a
308	// new source rather than mutating one, so nothing is shared with a command
309	// already in flight (Rule 110).
310	func (m Model) toggleTimestamps() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
311		src, ok := m.timestamps()
312		if !ok {
313			return m, nil
314		}
315		m.showTimestamps = !m.showTimestamps
316		m.source = src.WithTimestamps(m.showTimestamps)
317		m.loading = true
318		return m, loadCmd(m.source)
319	}
320	
321	// toggleFollow is `F`. It re-reads the source on its own clock, into this pane.
322	//
323	// It used to be tea.ExecProcess over `docker logs -f`, and the defect that
324	// replaced it is worth keeping written down: the only way out of that process
325	// is ctrl+c, a suspended TUI does not intercept it, so it killed DevDesk and
326	// gave the terminal back in whatever mode the child had left it — after which
327	// keys stopped answering. A capability whose only exit kills the application is
328	// not one.
329	//
330	// The read is the one `ctrl+r` already does: same command, same message, same
331	// handler. Following is that key on a timer and nothing more, which is why it
332	// costs no new loading path.
333	func (m Model) toggleFollow() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
334		src, ok := m.followable()
335		if !ok {
336			return m, nil
337		}
338		if m.following {
339			return m.stopFollowing(), nil
340		}
341		m.following = true
342		m.followGen++
343		// The first read is immediate. Waiting a whole interval before anything
344		// moves would leave the user unsure the key did anything, and what is on
345		// screen is already up to one interval old.
346		return m, tea.Batch(loadCmd(m.source), followTickCmd(src.FollowInterval(), m.followGen))
347	}
348	
349	// stopFollowing is the one place following is turned off, so no path can leave
350	// the flag set with no tick behind it, or a tick running with the flag clear.
351	func (m Model) stopFollowing() Model {
352		m.following = false
353		// Bumping the generation is what actually ends the loop. The tick already
354		// in flight blocks for its whole interval and arrives whatever happens
355		// here; the mismatch is what makes it a no-op instead of it finding the
356		// flag turned back on and carrying a second loop into the new run.
357		m.followGen++
358		return m
359	}
360	
361	// handleFollowTick re-reads, then schedules the next one.
362	//
363	// A stale tick — from a loop the user stopped, or restarted — returns no
364	// command, which is how the old loop dies rather than running beside the new.
365	func (m Model) handleFollowTick(msg followTickMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
366		if !m.following || msg.gen != m.followGen || m.source == nil {
367			return m, nil
368		}
369		src, ok := m.followable()
370		if !ok {
371			return m.stopFollowing(), nil
372		}
373		// m.loading stays false deliberately: a load is reported in the footer with
374		// a spinner (Rule 139), and one blinking every two seconds would read as
375		// something going wrong with the thing that is working. The follow status
376		// line is what says the pane is live.
377		return m, tea.Batch(loadCmd(m.source), followTickCmd(src.FollowInterval(), msg.gen))
378	}
379	
380	// openPager hands the document to the system pager.
381	//
382	// It survives for one source and deliberately: `less` handles a gigabyte and
383	// follows it, which a viewport holding the whole document in memory never will.
384	// Every other pager path in the application is gone.
385	func (m Model) openPager() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
386		src, ok := m.pageable()
387		if !ok {
388			return m, nil
389		}
390		return m, tea.ExecProcess(src.PagerCmd(), func(err error) tea.Msg {
391			return PagerExitMsg{Err: err}
392		})
393	}

1	package viewer
2	
3	import (
4		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/command"
5		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/viewer"
6	)
7	
8	// OpenRequestMsg asks the router to open a document. It is what every producer
9	// emits — workspaces for a file, containers for an inspect or a log — and the
10	// only thing they have to agree on.
11	//
12	// It carries the source rather than the content: the read happens in the
13	// viewer's own Init, so one place decides what is too large or not text, and one
14	// place reports it. A producer that loaded the bytes itself would each have to
15	// answer that question again, and answer it the same way.
16	type OpenRequestMsg struct {
17		Source viewer.Source
18	}
19	
20	// DocumentLoadedMsg carries the result of a Load back into Update (Rule 110).
21	type DocumentLoadedMsg struct {
22		Name    string
23		Kind    viewer.Kind
24		Content []byte
25		Err     error
26	}
27	
28	// BackToOriginMsg asks the router to return to the view the document was opened
29	// from. It mirrors security.BackToOriginMsg, and for the same reason: the view
30	// knows where it came from, the router knows how to get there.
31	type BackToOriginMsg struct {
32		Origin command.ViewType
33	}
34	
35	// PagerExitMsg comes back when the system pager or the follow process ends.
36	type PagerExitMsg struct {
37		Err error
38	}

1	package viewer
2	
3	import (
4		"os/exec"
5		"path/filepath"
6		"time"
7	)
8	
9	// Source is where a document came from, and it is carried rather than the bytes
10	// alone.
11	//
12	// The reason is everything the container logs pane could do that a byte slice
13	// cannot: reload, follow, re-fetch with timestamps. Those are properties of the
14	// *origin*, not of the pane — and a file gains from it too, since a document
15	// re-read after an external edit is the same question as a log re-fetched.
16	type Source interface {
17		// Name is what the header shows.
18		Name() string
19		// Kind is what the producer declares. KindAuto lets the name and the
20		// content decide, which is what a file browser passes.
21		Kind() Kind
22		// Load fetches the content. It runs on a Cmd's goroutine, never in Update
23		// (Rule 110).
24		Load() ([]byte, error)
25	}
26	
27	// The three optional capabilities below are probed with a type assertion, the
28	// same way the router probes FooterView and FramelessView.
29	//
30	// Each is a *single* method on purpose. CLAUDE.md's warning about HeaderView is
31	// that a view supplying two of its four methods satisfies none of it and fails
32	// in silence; an interface with one method has no half-satisfied state to fall
33	// into. That is why these are three interfaces and not one with three methods.
34	
35	// Timestamped is a source that can re-fetch with or without timestamps. It
36	// unlocks `t`.
37	type Timestamped interface {
38		Source
39		WithTimestamps(on bool) Source
40	}
41	
42	// Followable is a source worth re-reading on a clock. It unlocks `F`.
43	//
44	// It returns an interval rather than a command, and that is the whole of the
45	// fix. Following used to hand the terminal to `docker logs -f` through
46	// tea.ExecProcess, and there is no way out of that process but ctrl+c — which
47	// the suspended TUI does not intercept, so it killed DevDesk outright and left
48	// the terminal in whatever mode the child had put it in. Keys stopped answering
49	// afterwards. Observed, not theorised.
50	//
51	// A follow is therefore a re-read on a timer, inside the viewport, which is
52	// exactly what the ports tab already does with `ss`. The source names the
53	// cadence because only it knows what a read costs: a `docker logs --tail 500`
54	// is not a file stat.
55	//
56	// The trade is stated rather than discovered: this polls, it does not stream.
57	// A line can wait up to one interval, and a burst longer than the source's tail

68	// Two seconds, the ports tab's cadence, and for the same reason: it is about
69	// the slowest a live pane can refresh and still read as live. A re-read is one
70	// `docker logs --tail 500` — the very exec `ctrl+r` already runs — so following
71	// costs one process every two seconds while the user is watching it, and
72	// nothing at all once they stop.

99	// escaping — it sees the backslashes as part of the path. The result was

101	// name or volume label syntax is incorrect", and the pager returning to DevDesk

103	// string through exec.Command.

106	// `more` reads a pipe perfectly well — `dir | more` is its canonical use — so
107	// the two branches now differ only in the shell and the pager's name. Nothing
108	// is written to disk, and no path needs quoting.
109	//
110	// The container ID is interpolated into a shell string, which is only safe
111	// because it comes from `docker ps`. Do not extend this to a value the user
112	// types.
113	func (s logsSource) PagerCmd() *exec.Cmd {

content.text:
J'ai ajouté les deux raccourcis dans le viewer :

- **`Y`** — copie le texte source du document ouvert dans le presse-papiers (pas ce que `f` affiche : un Markdown rendu copie quand même ses marqueurs bruts).
- **`O`** — ouvre le fichier dans l'IDE configuré (`app.ide_command`). N'apparaît que si la source est un vrai fichier sur disque (nouvelle interface `viewer.Pathed`) — un `docker inspect` ou des logs de conteneur n'ont pas de chemin à ouvrir.

Détails techniques :
- `internal/viewer/source.go` : nouvelle interface `Pathed` (méthode `Path()`), implémentée par `FileSource`.
- `internal/ui/viewer/update.go` : gestion des touches `keymap.Copy`/`keymap.IDE`, nouveaux messages `ContentCopiedMsg`/`IDEOpenedMsg`, erreurs reportées dans le footer (Rule 128).
- `internal/ui/viewer/view.go` : entrées ajoutées dans `GetShortcuts()` (Rule 130, conditionnées à la présence d'un document / d'un chemin) et `GetHelpContent()`.
- La description globale de `Y` dans `internal/ui/keymap/keymap.go` a été généralisée ("copie le chemin, ou le contenu d'un document") puisqu'elle ne copiait jusqu'ici qu'un chemin.
- Un test de `workspaces` utilisait le champ `FileSource.Path` directement — corrigé pour utiliser la nouvelle méthode `Path()`.

Build, `go vet`, tests (`go test ./...`) et `golangci-lint` passent tous. Pas de commit fait — dis-moi si tu veux que je committe/ouvre une PR (ce projet exige un worktree dédié pour ça).
